title: Hiring debrief for the data engineer role

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Hi, can everyone hear me?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yes, hi Camille.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Loud and clear.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Hi Camille, sorry, I'm here. Just closing my other window.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Hi, Marisol. Okay, so this is the debrief for the data engineer role. We saw two final candidates this week, Aarav Chaturvedi and Yusuf Demirci. Imogen, could you start with where things stand, and then we'll hear from Kwabena and Marisol?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Sure. Both candidates finished all four interviews, and both are still very interested. Two practical things. Yusuf told me yesterday he has another offer, and they want an answer by Monday. Aarav doesn't have another offer that I know of, but he's at Acme and his notice period is three months.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Three months? That's long.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: It is. He thinks Acme might let him go earlier, but I wouldn't count on it.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay. Kwabena, you ran the technical interview. What did you think?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Honestly, Yusuf was the strongest technical candidate I've seen this year. On the design exercise he redrew our whole pipeline, found the two places where we lose data when a job restarts, and suggested a fix I'd already considered and thrown away, except his version actually works. Aarav was good too. Solid, no real mistakes. But he didn't go as deep, and when I asked about streaming data, he told me himself he'd only done it on side projects.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Thanks, Kwabena. Marisol?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: I see it a bit differently. I agree Yusuf is brilliant technically, nobody's arguing with that. But in the team interview he barely asked a single question. When I asked how he'd explain a delay to the analysts, he said he'd send them the logs. Aarav asked about every person on the team, how the analysts work, what they complain about. This person will sit between engineering and the analysts all day. That part of the job matters at least as much as the code.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: It matters, but the reason we're hiring is that the pipelines keep breaking.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: The pipelines keep breaking partly because nobody talks to the analysts before changing things, Kwabena.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: That's not fair.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Okay, that came out wrong. Sorry. What I mean is, half our incidents last quarter started with a change nobody announced.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: That part's true. I'll give you that.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Can I ask something? Kwabena, if we hire Aarav, what's the risk, concretely?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: That I spend the first six months teaching him streaming instead of building things. It's teachable. It's just slow.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: And Marisol, if we hire Yusuf?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: That we fix the pipelines and the analysts still don't trust them. And that I spend six months coaching him on how to talk to people, which is much harder to teach.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Can I add one thing from my side, Camille?

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Sorry, go ahead, Imogen.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yusuf's references are excellent, but two of them mentioned the same thing Marisol did. Great engineer, prefers to work alone. Aarav's manager at Acme called him the person everyone goes to with questions.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: References always say nice things.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: They do, which is exactly why I noticed when two of them said the same less nice thing.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Fair point, Imogen.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay. Money. Imogen, are they both inside the salary band?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yusuf is, just. Aarav asked for about eight thousand above the top of the band. Keziah Ashdown would have to approve that.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Keziah approved more than that for the analytics lead in the spring.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: She did, but she wasn't happy about it. I'd want a strong case.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Let me tell you where I am, and then you can push back. I think Marisol is right about the role. This team needs someone who connects people. But Kwabena's worry is real, and I don't want to discover a gap in the first month. So I'd like to make an offer to Aarav, but only after one more hour with Kwabena on streaming. If that goes well, we offer. If it doesn't, we come back to Yusuf.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Yusuf won't wait. His other offer runs out on Monday.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: I know. That's the cost of this choice, and I accept it.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I don't love it, to be honest. I think we'll regret losing him.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: We might. But we'd regret the other choice more.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Maybe. You're the one who'll manage him, Marisol, so I'll respect that. But I want it in the notes that I preferred Yusuf.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: It's in the notes, Kwabena. Thank you for saying it clearly.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: So what do I tell Yusuf?

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: The truth, Imogen. That he was very strong, that we chose someone else for the role, and that we'd like to stay in touch. If a second position opens next year, he's the first call.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Okay, Camille. I'll call him rather than email.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Thank you. Now the actions. Kwabena, can you do the extra hour with Aarav this week?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Thursday afternoon works. I'll keep it practical. One real streaming problem from our backlog, nothing he could prepare for.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Not a trick question, please.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: No tricks, Marisol, I promise. A real problem.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Imogen, can you set that up with Aarav and prepare the salary case for Keziah?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yes. I'll book Thursday today, and I'll send the case to Keziah Ashdown by Friday morning, so she can answer before the weekend. I'll copy Marisol Echeverría, since she'll be his manager.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: And I'll write to Aarav after the interview, whatever happens. I want him to know who he'd be working with.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Good. And if Kwabena Mensah says no on Thursday, we meet again on Friday at nine and decide about Yusuf, even if it means asking him for a few more days.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: That's fair, Camille. Thanks.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I'll put Friday at nine in everyone's calendar, just in case.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Perfect. Anything else before we go?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Only that they were both really good, and that's a nice problem to have.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Agreed.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Thanks, everyone. Talk on Thursday.
